beats.narration_text: This video was built by the skill it explains. The ai-explainer skill turns a Claude concept or a SKILL.md file into a narrated educational video. If you are teaching teammates how to use Claude — or documenting a workflow you've built — this skill is the pipeline. Here is how it works, when to reach for it, and what it will not do.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. The ai-explainer folder is one file — SKILL.md, roughly fourteen kilobytes. That file declares everything: the fidelity palette, the channel table, the ILLUSTRATE law, the GATE P pedagogy check, and the skill-teardown modifier. You point it at content; it returns a beat sheet. The folder is the contract between the human and the machine.

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: Declared inside: channels · palette laws · ILLUSTRATE law · GATE P · modifiers
props.calloutSub: Old name: claude-explainer (renamed: vendor names aren't skill identities)

beats.narration_text: Five stages. Beat sheet: Claude authors structured narration in your chosen register. GATE P: a human signs off before any audio generation — no spend without approval. Audio: Kokoro narration, locally generated and measured. Measured durations become the master clock. Visuals: Remotion scenes, Manim fragments, and code blocks, all sized to the audio. Compile: a finished mp4. One invariant governs everything: audio first. Duration is a measured output, never a fixed input.

beats.narration_text: Here is the method demonstrated. The skill cannot recurse on itself — that loops — so it runs on its nearest sibling, sketch-explainer. Command: ./art ai-explainer skills/make/sketch-explainer/SKILL.md. Claude reads the entire SKILL.md. It writes an eleven-beat script. The pedagogy check runs. Audio is queued. One argument, no configuration.

beats.narration_text: The output is a beat sheet. Each beat has three required fields: beat id, narration, and shot definition. The shot definition names the Remotion component and its props. The metadata block sets the brand: voice, palette, channel. That file is what the machine returns from one command. What remains for the human: listen to the audio, check the narration against the visual, watch the frames. The script is the draft; the human is the editor.

props.title: beat_sheet.json — ai-explainer output

beats.narration_text: The ILLUSTRATE law governs the middle beats. The Claude composer window appears in exactly five places per video: cold open, ask micro-beats, verdict page, handoff, and outro. Every other beat must illustrate its concept — a Remotion diagram, a Manim fragment, or a code block. The law exists because a reel of composer windows teaches nothing about the subject. In practice: if your beat sheet has the same visual pattern in two consecutive beats, redesign the second one.

props.heading: The UI earns its appearances.
props.body: Five appearances only: cold open · ask micro-beats · verdict page · handoff · outro. Every other inner beat illustrates — Remotion diagram, Manim fragment, or code block.
props.quote: Two consecutive beats on the same visual scheme is the smell; a reel of composer wallpaper is the failure this law prevents.

beats.narration_text: The skill-teardown modifier activates when your source is a SKILL.md file. You do not invoke it by name. What it adds: an anatomy beat mapping the folder, a pipeline beat diagramming the build, two to four mechanism acts for the key laws, and a design tell. The self-demo law follows from it: the reel must run the skill it explains. Real output only. A fabricated demo is an explicit DOUBLE-CHECK LAW violation — the SKILL.md names it as such.

props.heading: Modifier activates on SKILL.md source.
props.body: Source is SKILL.md → modifier arms without being named. Adds: anatomy · pipeline · 2–4 mechanism acts · design tell · self-demo (real output required).
props.quote: A faked demo is a DOUBLE-CHECK LAW violation, not a shortcut.

beats.narration_text: The fidelity constraint: the palette replicates the actual Claude application interface. Cream page, warm ink, one terracotta accent. The constraint is not aesthetic. The skill's own rule is strict: the moment the visual drifts from the real product, the skill loses its reason to exist. If you are building a Claude-branded video, do not retheme it. The channel is the brand; the palette is fixed.

props.heading: Palette is fixed.
props.body: Cream page, warm ink, terracotta accent — the real Claude app interface by design. The channel is the brand; the palette is the contract.
props.quote: The moment it stops looking like the actual Claude app it loses its reason to exist.

beats.narration_text: Method summary. The ai-explainer skill runs on three fixed rules: fidelity palette, Teardown register, and the ILLUSTRATE law. On a SKILL.md source, the teardown modifier activates automatically — anatomy, pipeline, mechanism acts, design tell, and a required self-demo. The ILLUSTRATE law limits the Claude interface to five appearances. The fidelity rule ties the palette to the real product. What breaks: two consecutive beats with the same visual scheme, a fabricated demo, or a palette that drifts. Command: ./art ai-explainer your-source.

ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude interface earns exactly five appearances. Every other beat illustrates its concept natively.
What breaks: repeated visual scheme in consecutive beats, a fabricated demo, or a palette that drifts from the real app.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read this with me. 'Use the ai-explainer skill on a SKILL.md from a project you are working on. Pick the mechanism your team consistently misunderstands. The pedagogy gate stops you before any spend. If you cannot produce a working demo, the skill will say so — do not substitute a description for the demo.' Paste that into Claude Code. Point it at a real SKILL.md. The machine will flag what it cannot build. Your job is to supply it.

props.command: Use the ai-explainer skill on a SKILL.md from your project. Pick the mechanism your team misunderstands. The pedagogy gate stops you before any spend. If you can't produce a working demo, flag the gap — do not fabricate the demo.

beats.narration_text: Three commands to start. First: ./art keys — validates every credential before any spend. Second: ./art ai-explainer skills/make/your-skill/SKILL.md — runs the skill on a SKILL.md from your own project. Third: ./art todo your-reel-path — shows what the machine built and what it left for you. That third command is where the human work begins.

props.title: Three commands.
props.code:
# 1. validate credentials before any spend
./art keys

# 2. run the skill on your SKILL.md
./art ai-explainer skills/make/<your-skill>/SKILL.md

# 3. see what the machine filled — and what it left
./art todo <your-reel-path>
